  1. 1.dr-statusbarThe status bar: 44 tall, 9:41 and three 17px system glyphs in --ink. It depicts what iOS draws; the product owns none of it.
  2. 2.dr-brandThe brand slot: the DRON quadcopter mark as a 60 × 20 CSS mask in the bar's ink, role="img" aria-label="DRON", 15.99:1 on the page.
  3. 3.dr-topbar__titleThe screen's one name: an <h1>, 17/600/−0.01em, centred absolutely in the 56px nav bar, 15.99:1.
  4. 4.dr-mainThe scrolling column between the bars. See Screen layout.
  5. 5.dr-tab[aria-current="page"]The selected tab: a --green-wash pill at radius 16 behind an --ink icon and label, 14.75:1. Target 86.3 × 50.
  6. 6.dr-homeThe home indicator: a 30px band holding a 134 × 5 bar in --ink.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Nav bar; Status bar; Tab bar; Home indicator; Brand slot; Back button.

When to use

Every product screen stands in this frame: status bar 44, nav bar 56, then either a tab bar (60 + 30) on a tab root or an action bar on a pushed screen. Every bar takes the page ground --page and only a 1px hairline separates it from the content. The client's tabs are Order · Activity · Help · Account; the operator's are Jobs · Earnings · Ratings · Account.

The selected tab carries the accent as a fill, not as a tinted label. HIG tints the label with the accent, but raw green as text is 1.69:1, so the accent moves into the pill and the ink darkens with it: two signals where the convention gives one.

The nav bar holds one name: the title of the screen you are on, in sentence case. The back control carries no words (microcopy.md D9); Back to… is right as an accessible name and forbidden as visible copy. A tab root has no back. listings-filters is the one deliberate exception: a × with aria-label="Close filters", because a sheet is dismissed rather than a screen popped.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Navigation · voice.md § Nav-bar back button · microcopy.md D9 · inventory.md § 1 (Nav bar, Status bar, Tab bar, Home indicator, Brand slot, Back button)

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Rate the order

The nav bar of rate: the chevron alone, named for assistive tech by where it goes, and one title in the centre.

Don’t

‹ Delivered

Rate the order

A labelled back button puts a second screen name in the bar, and the two read as two titles rather than a control and a name. Use .dr-back with the chevron alone and the destination in aria-label. A filled disc does not belong in the bar either: a trailing control is a bare glyph, like the notification bell, or a word, like a text button.
